subject: Post-call: Dedicated + Integration follow-ups and clarifications
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@finharvest.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finharvest.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 10:14:00 -0400
Subject: Post-call: Dedicated + Integration follow-ups and clarifications

Hi Jordan & Priya —

Thanks for the productive call this morning. Per our discussion, I wanted to summarize the open technical points so your engineering team can review and we can lock a concrete POC scope. I’ve split items into Integration (SDK/auth/routing), Model features (structured output/tool-calling, embeddings/rerank), and Dedicated capacity sizing (throughput, concurrency, autoscale).

Integration / SDK & auth
- SDK setup: you will use our Python SDK for the POC (we also have Node/Java). We’ll share a minimal example that demonstrates streaming + KV cache reuse.
- Auth: standard API key for Hosted. For Dedicated we recommend mTLS to the customer-managed gateway; we support API keys backed by KMS for HSM integrations.
- Routing: primary routing policy during POC will be latency-first to the dedicated pool with fallback to hosted if capacity constrained; we can configure weighted routing if you want cost fallbacks.

Model features
- Structured output / tool calling: Redwood supports JSON schema enforcement + function calling. For FinHarvest’s parser, we recommend a structured-output schema for transaction extraction (examples attached).
- Embeddings & rerank: we suggest generating embeddings client-side via the SDK and using our batch embedding endpoint. Reranking in the POC: run a small candidate generation step in your infra and call our rerank endpoint for final ordering.

Dedicated sizing & ops
- Target throughput you mentioned: ~200 requests/minute peak, average 60/min. Typical prompt length ~400 tokens; response ~200 tokens.
- Concurrency: we recommend reserving a concurrency window of 40 active requests per GPU node initially; autoscale policy to add nodes at 70% node utilization.
- Queues: use a short-lived priority queue for low-latency flows and a background queue (batching enabled) for non-urgent bulk enrichment.

Next steps (action items)
1) I’ll send the SDK snippet + auth diagrams and the draft sizing proposal (attached). — Camila (today EOD)
2) Jordan/Priya: share an anonymized sample of 50 typical prompts + token counts so we can validate throughput assumptions. (Target: by next Tue)
3) Internal: Vivek & Marissa to confirm SLA / fallback behaviors and suggest autoscale thresholds. — Camila

Open questions for your team
- Do you need support for on-prem model hosting for data residency during the POC, or will Dedicated in your VPC suffice?
- For reranking latency SLO, is 150–200ms acceptable for the final ranking call?

Thanks again — attaching a quick diagram and the sizing draft. Happy to hop on another 30m with your infra leads if helpful.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing-proposal.pdf (15KB stub), sample-auth-flows.drawio (2KB stub)

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@finharvest.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finharvest.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 10:47:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: Dedicated + Integration follow-ups and clarifications

Thanks Camila — helpful summary. A few clarifying questions from our engineering side before we gather the sample prompts: 

1) Auth & mTLS: for Dedicated in our VPC, will we need to terminate mTLS at our ingress and then use a Redwood sidecar, or can we terminate at your gateway with client certs? We’d prefer minimal network plumbing.

2) Embeddings: you mentioned batch embedding endpoint — any guidance on batch size limits and response latency? We’ll likely embed ~5k docs (average 250 tokens) during ingestion.

3) Rerank latency: 150–200ms is fine for interactive flows, but for micro-batch enrichment we can tolerate higher. For the POC, can you put a priority cap so rerank calls are routed to higher-priority nodes?

I’ll get the sample prompts over to you by Monday. Also please confirm whether the sizing PDF you attached assumes 1 or 2 GPUs per node.

— Jordan

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@finharvest.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finharvest.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 11:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: Dedicated + Integration follow-ups and clarifications

Jordan — answers inline below. Also pasted some minimal examples at the bottom for SDK/auth.

1) mTLS termination: two supported patterns
  - Minimal plumbing (recommended for POC): Redwood terminates mTLS at our customer-dedicated gateway. You present client certs; we authenticate, then forward over internal secure links to the pool in your VPC. This avoids running a sidecar.
  - Sidecar (if you want fully customer-controlled egress): terminate at your ingress and use the Redwood sidecar to manage secrets and route to our control plane.

2) Embeddings: batch endpoint guidance:
  - Recommended batch size: 64–512 vectors per call depending on average token length; you’ll likely do 64–128 for 250-token docs to balance memory and latency.
  - Ingestion throughput: use streaming uploads + client-side micro-batching; we can process 200–300 docs/sec across a dedicated 4×A100 pool in warm state (depends on quantization). We’ll validate with your sample.

3) Rerank priority cap: yes — we support priority routing tags. For the POC we can route rerank calls with tag "high-priority" to a reserved slice (approx 20% of capacity) to ensure <200ms p95 when under typical load.

SDK snippets (Python) — minimal auth example:
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED")
# streaming example
with client.chat.stream(model="rwd-gtp-m-7b", input="Summarize the transaction...") as stream:
    for chunk in stream:
        print(chunk.text, end='')

Attachments: I’ll update the sizing PDF to note GPU-per-node assumptions (current draft assumes 1×A100 per node for conservative estimates).

If it helps, Vivek can write up the SLA + autoscale constraints so you have explicit failure/fallback behaviour documented.

Best,
Camila

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@finharvest.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 15:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: Dedicated + Integration follow-ups and clarifications

Adding a few ops-focused constraints from the Dedicated SLA / infra perspective:

- Autoscale policy: start scale-up when avg GPU utilization > 70% for 120s; scale-down only when < 35% for 300s to avoid flapping. For the POC we recommend a minimum pool size of 2 nodes (safety) and a max of 6 nodes.
- Concurrency limits: set per-node soft concurrency 40 requests; hard cap 56 to prevent OOMs when under unusual token spikes.
- Queueing behavior: low-latency queue should have a short timeout (1.5s wait); if a request times out, it should be retried with exponential backoff or fall back to hosted routing depending on policy.
- Monitoring / alerts: we will provide per-route token/latency dashboards and an incident webhook. Please let us know which Slack channel or PagerDuty escalation you want us to push to during the POC.

I’ll coordinate with Marissa to add these thresholds into the final proposal doc and call out expected unit cost delta for reserved capacity vs hosted fallback.

— Vivek

Thanks Camila & Vivek — that addresses our immediate questions.

Action items from our side:
- We’ll share the anonymized sample prompts (50) by Monday and include token counts.
- We prefer Redwood terminating mTLS at the dedicated gateway for the POC (minimal plumbing).
- Confirmed: we want the reserved rerank slice for priority calls.

Next step: Priya will schedule a 30m POC kickoff with our infra and security leads for Tuesday 2026-06-02 at 11:00 AM ET. Please include the updated sizing PDF and the SLA section Vivek mentioned.

Looking forward to the POC.

— Jordan
